teamLeadership.label: Team Leadership
teamLeadership.description: Lead team meetings and manage conflicts

customerService.question: An irate customer says their order arrived damaged. What's your first move?

options.A: Listen fully, acknowledge the problem and apologize sincerely.
options.B: Immediately offer a refund just to end the call quickly.
options.C: Ask them to email photos before you'll do anything.
options.D: Explain that damage in transit isn't your company's fault.

customerService.question: The customer is still upset after your apology. How do you proceed?

options.A: Ask what outcome would make things right for them.
options.B: Restate the policy and wait for them to accept it.
options.C: Transfer them to a supervisor to avoid the conflict.
options.D: Put them on a long hold to let them cool down.

customerService.question: You've agreed on a replacement. How do you set expectations?

options.A: Give a clear timeline and a way to track it.
options.B: Promise it 'as soon as possible' with no specifics.
options.C: Say you'll 'try', but make no real commitment.
options.D: Overpromise next-day delivery you can't guarantee.

customerService.question: The issue is resolved. How do you prevent a repeat?

options.A: Log the root cause and flag the packaging problem.
options.B: Close the ticket and move on to the next call.
options.C: Blame the courier in your notes and leave it.
options.D: Add a private note to avoid this customer next time.

teamLeadership.question: Two team members start arguing openly in your meeting. What do you do?

options.A: Pause and set a respectful ground rule before continuing.
options.B: Take the side of whoever is technically correct.
options.C: Ignore it and push through the agenda.
options.D: End the meeting abruptly to stop the tension.

teamLeadership.question: After the meeting, how do you address the conflict?

options.A: Meet each person privately to understand their view.
options.B: Send a group email telling everyone to stay professional.
options.C: Wait and hope it resolves itself.
options.D: Reassign one of them to a different team.

teamLeadership.question: You've heard both sides. How do you move forward?

options.A: Facilitate a joint conversation focused on shared goals.
options.B: Impose a solution and expect everyone to comply.
options.C: Let the more senior person decide for the group.
options.D: Avoid the topic entirely to keep the peace.

teamLeadership.question: How do you prevent clashes like this in future?

options.A: Agree on team norms for handling disagreement together.
options.B: Add more status meetings to keep an eye on things.
options.C: Monitor their messages closely for tension.
options.D: Assume it was a one-off and do nothing.

salesNegotiation.question: A prospect loves the product but says your price is too high. Your response?

options.A: Ask what value or budget target they're working toward.
options.B: Immediately drop the price to win the deal.
options.C: Insist the price is final and non-negotiable.
options.D: Criticize competitors' cheaper offers.

salesNegotiation.question: They reveal a limited budget. How do you proceed?

options.A: Propose a scoped package that fits their budget.
options.B: Give them the full product at a loss.
options.C: Walk away from the deal on the spot.
options.D: Hide some fees to make the price look lower.

salesNegotiation.question: They ask for one more concession before signing. What do you do?

options.A: Trade the concession for a longer commitment.
options.B: Give it away for free to avoid any friction.
options.C: Refuse flatly and hold your position.
options.D: Agree verbally but leave it out of the contract.

salesNegotiation.question: The deal is nearly closed. How do you finalize it?

options.A: Confirm all terms in writing and set next steps.
options.B: Rush the signature before they change their mind.
options.C: Leave the details vague to close faster.
options.D: Add a few surprise terms at the moment of signing.

projectManagement.question: Your project is falling behind schedule. What is your immediate action?

options.A: Assess the root cause with the team before reacting.
options.B: Inform stakeholders about the delay transparently.
options.C: Reassign the work to a different team.
options.D: Pressure the team to work overtime.

projectManagement.question: How do you handle the team's response to your decision?

options.A: Hold an open meeting to discuss the situation together.
options.B: Send an email update and wait for replies.
options.C: Meet team leads individually to gather detail.
options.D: Let the team figure it out on their own.

projectManagement.question: What's your approach to stakeholder communication?

options.A: Share a revised timeline with clear milestones.
options.B: Provide detailed weekly progress reports.
options.C: Call an urgent crisis meeting with everyone.
options.D: Minimize communication to avoid causing panic.

projectManagement.question: How do you ensure recovery and prevent a repeat?

options.A: Run a post-mortem and adjust the process.
options.B: Add resources without changing how you work.
options.C: Impose rigid new controls immediately.
options.D: Move on and focus on the next project.

conflictResolution.question: Two departments blame each other for a missed handoff. Your first step?

options.A: Gather the facts from both sides neutrally.
options.B: Decide who's at fault from first impressions.
options.C: Escalate to senior management immediately.
options.D: Tell them to sort it out among themselves.

conflictResolution.question: Emotions are running high in the room. How do you manage the discussion?

options.A: Set ground rules and focus on the problem, not the people.
options.B: Let everyone vent freely with no structure.
options.C: Cut the discussion short to save time.
options.D: Side with whichever group is louder.

conflictResolution.question: You've found the root cause. How do you resolve it?

options.A: Agree on a shared fix with clear ownership.
options.B: Assign blame and require an apology.
options.C: Add a rule without addressing the real cause.
options.D: Paper over it just to keep the peace.

conflictResolution.question: How do you rebuild trust between the teams?

options.A: Set up a shared process and a follow-up check-in.
options.B: Keep the teams apart to avoid more friction.
options.C: Reorganize the reporting lines instead.
options.D: Assume trust will simply return on its own.

presentation.question: You're about to pitch a proposal to skeptical executives. How do you open?

options.A: Lead with the problem and the outcome they care about.
options.B: Start with a long company-history slide.
options.C: Open by apologizing for taking their time.
options.D: Dive straight into deep technical detail.

presentation.question: An executive interrupts with a tough question. What do you do?

options.A: Answer directly, then return to your thread.
options.B: Deflect and say you'll cover it later (then don't).
options.C: Guess an answer to sound confident.
options.D: Get defensive about being interrupted.

presentation.question: You're running short on time. How do you adapt?

options.A: Skip to your key ask and the evidence for it.
options.B: Speed-read through every remaining slide.
options.C: Drop the ask entirely to save time.
options.D: Run over and ignore the clock.

presentation.question: You've finished presenting. How do you close?

options.A: Restate the ask and propose a clear next step.
options.B: End with a vague 'so, that's it, thanks'.
options.C: Leave without any call to action.
options.D: Promise to 'send everything over sometime'.

generic.question: What is your immediate course of action?

options.A: Assess the situation and gather the facts first.
options.B: Communicate openly with the people affected.
options.C: Delegate the whole problem to someone else.
options.D: Act quickly without consulting anyone.

generic.question: How do you involve the people affected?

options.A: Ask for their input before you decide.
options.B: Inform them once you've already decided.
options.C: Keep them out of it to move faster.
options.D: Leave them to handle it entirely alone.

generic.question: How do you communicate your plan?

options.A: Share clear steps, owners and timelines.
options.B: Give a rough idea and adjust as you go.
options.C: Say as little as possible for now.
options.D: Overpromise to reassure everyone.

generic.question: How do you prevent the problem from recurring?

options.A: Review what happened and improve the process.
options.B: Add controls without diagnosing the cause.
options.C: Move on and hope it doesn't happen again.
options.D: Blame external factors and leave it there.
